answer: Hedge funds may restrict when you can get your money back. They typically allow redemptions four times a year or fewer, and often have a lock-up period of one year or more when you cannot cash in your shares. Some funds may also charge a redemption fee or suspend redemptions in certain circumstances. These limits mean you should understand when and how you can redeem before investing.
